items.title: The time word sits at the end
items.caption: The complete sentence comes first. The time word added at the tail says when the whole event happened.

items.title: The front of the word points through time
items.caption: The shared root names morning. The front *ana-* looks back, while *ʻā-* looks ahead.

items.title: Sort time gone by and time ahead
items.intro: Place each time word on the side of now that it points toward.

items.why: The *ana-* front points back to time already gone.
This is one of the chapter's time words for the past.
Earlier today is already behind the moment of speaking.
This word reaches back to a former time.
The *ʻā-* front points ahead to the coming morning.
This fixed time word points ahead.
